title: The suggestions section — read a row, write a verdict, and only then does anyone build it
review_protocol: 1. each row states the decision a reviewer must make, the options with what each one costs and locks, and the evidence that narrows them
2. `verdict` is blank on every row by design; the only thing that turns a suggestion into work is a verdict written into this file (option letter, or 'reject' + reason)
3. a session may implement a row only when its verdict is non-blank and its commit records the verdict; nothing in this namespace is implemented
4. `basis` names the kind of evidence behind the recommendation (official read / repo computation / gate arithmetic) so a reviewer can see when the recommendation is only a judgement
scope_note: This register consolidates the decision surface across the repository rather than repeating it. The census on pages/consolidation.html is computed from every committed register by engine/inventory.py at commit b340a49: 20 peer suggestion registers hold 156 rows in 19 namespaces, 18 question registers hold 184 rows, 23 flag registers hold 176 rows and 12 requirement registers hold 456 rows. If that commit is no longer current, the census page moves with the next inventory refresh and this sentence is re-checked against it; rows below that echo a peer proposal say so in `evidence`, and the new material is this session's official reads and the arithmetic they force.
